required_outcomes: Recognises the gas escape has been made safe (cooker capped and labelled, boiler and meter checked) and moves the job to an urgent Gas Safe repair of the cooker rather than an emergency.

Arranges a Gas Safe registered engineer to repair or replace the capped cooker and look at the oven heating fault, or routes the job to provider selection with the Gas Safe requirement recorded when no Gas Safe contractor is on file.
Replies to the tenant: thanks her, keep the cooker capped and do not use it or remove the label, a Gas Safe engineer is being arranged, and get in touch or call 0800 111 999 if the smell returns.
Updates the landlord with the gas emergency service findings and that a Gas Safe engineer is needed, seeking approval for the repair cost where it is not already in place.
acceptable_alternatives: Requesting the landlord's approval for the Gas Safe engineer and putting the job on hold for the landlord with a short review date, provided the tenant and landlord are both updated.
A P2 or P3 note to the maintenance team about the urgent cooker repair, if the routine work is also done.
positive_behaviours: Treats the repair as urgent (within days), since the tenant has no oven or hob.
Notes the oven fault may share a cause with the leak so the engineer checks both.
Asks the landlord whether a gas safety record for the property is current.
red_flags: Raises a new P1 escalation or repeats the evacuation advice as if the leak were still live.
Sends a general appliance repairer who is not Gas Safe registered.
prohibited_actions: Telling the tenant she can use the cooker or remove the cap or label.
Booking the repair as routine weeks away.
critical_failures: Leaving the capped cooker with no Gas Safe engineer arranged or requested and no next step for the landlord or provider selection.
